messages.subject: data going to wrong facet
parts:

particular facet are being placed in the wrong facet. What am I doing
wrong?

Here is a small sample of the data:

here's what I did:

mk<-read.table("mk.txt", header=T)
attach(mk)

qplot(start, FETpvalueM_MSmin2, facets=arm~., data=subset(mk,
FETpvalueM_MSmin2<0.05))+geom_text(label=file, size = 4, hjust = 1,

X, but this is not happening here. Instead, 'files' are being placed

1, :

Thanks, again.

messages.author: eca99c51870663ea
messages.subject: Re: data going to wrong facet
parts:
This is probably very basic information for many out there, but just in case...

To write out an object in a format that can be easily cut and pasted:
> dput(mk)
  [copy the output and paste into email message]

This generates output that the other person can just copy and paste into their R console to generate the correct data structure.


On the receiving end, even if the data has been pasted in a plain text format (as squid did earlier) rather than a nice R command format from dput(), it's still possible to read it in without too much trouble.
> mk <- read.table(file=stdin(), header=T)
 [paste table text here]

However, there's no guarantee that the types of each column will be correct; if the sender wants, for example, a column of numbers to be treated as a factor, that conversion needs to be done by hand.

-Winston

parts:
> I notice that R 2.9 for macs now has a stable release, so I will
> update that today although I can't imagine that is the problem.  In
> the updated ggplot2, I am still having the bizarre problem I report
> above.  Again, the example file is in the files section (mktest.txt)
> and when I type the following command, the data go to the wrong facets
> and have the wrong "start"
>
> qplot(start, FETpvalueM_MSmin2, data=subset(mk,
> FETpvalueM_MSmin2<0.05), facets=arm~.)+geom_text(label=file, size = 4,
> hjust = 1, vjust = 1,data=subset(mk, FETpvalueM_MSmin2<0.05))

Try this code:

qplot(start, FETpvalueM_MSmin2, facets = arm ~ ., data = mk) +
geom_text(aes(label=file), size = 4, hjust = 1, vjust = 1) +
ylim(0, 0.05)

The problem is that you were missing the aes call in geom_text and you
had previously used attach, so ggplot2 used the file variable from the
global environment, causing the issue you saw.


Hadley


--
